Code 57/1/1, BIOLOGY (Theory), 3 hours, 70 marks; internal job number 2401-1); idx 1 is the Hindi instructions; every ODD index 3-21 is the Hindi facing page and opens with a Hindi question number (checked on the contact sheet, the text layer's block order, and full size for idx 17 and 21), so no English overflows onto an odd page and the parity never inverts. idx 23 is blank apart from the footer. The paper is born-digital: the text layer was used as a DRAFT only and every row was checked against the full-size page (the layer drops the underline under 'not' in Q1, the Q9 column layout and the superscript in Ca++, and the q-squared superscripts in Q24). Instruction (viii) gives no count of internal choices; the roster was built from the marking scheme's bare ORs and confirmed against a printed OR on the page: Q18, Q20, Q21, Q29(a), Q30(a), Q31, Q32, Q33, eight alternatives, none in Section C. Primary marks: A16 + B10 + C21 + D8 + E15 = 70. Section-A key read off the scheme IMAGE (ms idx 2) and independently from the scheme's text layer: DCBBAAABCDBBACCD, 16 of 16 agree. No CBSE void anywhere in the scheme (the only award note, Q33(b)(ii), is conditional). Q32(b): the ENGLISH paper prints the coding strand ending '... GCA TTA 3'' while the HINDI page (idx 21) prints '... GCA TAA 3'' (a stop codon); the scheme follows the English. The paper prints no decimals, so the raised-dot rule never arises. Quotes are straight, scientific names plain text (the Biology rules).
